To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the information about the state of the world that is used to make decisions in an experiment is a function of the number of reports and the trustworthiness of the sources; and 2) the value of the information is a public good.

(i) the value of news is a special form of a public goods, and (ii) the value of the news is a function of the trust in its source, and (iii) the value of information in the presence of cascades depends on the value of the information to the decision maker, and (iv) the value of cascades depends upon both the trust in the source and the value of the decision.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of news in economic decision making, and the implications of the role for economic efficiency and social welfare.
the role of fake news in the aggregation of information and the implications for the economic value of the resulting information.
information aggregation and the economic implications of fake news.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of the experiment provide evidence of a strong and robust link between the economics and the psychology of decision making.
fake news" has the potential to distort the aggregation of information about the underlying state of the world and thereby distort decisions.
the experiments demonstrate how the value of news is a public good, and how the public good value of news depends on the credibility of the source of news.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the information aggregation process is dependent on the trustworthiness of news sources.
the value of news as a public goods is enhanced when news reports are more accurate, when there are more sources of news and when there is a greater diversity of news sources.
fake news is not a new phenomenon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
news is a public good and that the public nature of the good has implications for the efficiency of its production and consumption.
the public goods value of news is dependent on the quality of the information sources.
the value of news depends on the quality of the news sources and the quality of the information processing of readers.
